extracted.intended_audience: general readers and performers interested in comedy (especially insult comedy)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for the comedy genre where the act consists primarily of offensive insults directed at audiences, other performers, or roast subjects; notes typical targets and common uses (e.g., handling hecklers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Central defining characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: The act consists mainly of offensive insults, usually directed at the audience or other performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core definition of the genre: material is primarily composed of direct insults rather than narrative jokes, observational bits, or satire. The phrase comes verbatim from the lead description of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical targets for insult include people in the show's audience, the town hosting the performance, or the subject of a roast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting insult-comedy material, common acceptable targets include individual audience members, the local community/venue, or a named roast subject; targeting other performers is also typical. Examples given in the article emphasize audience, town, and roast-subject targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from satire and political humor
rubrics_metrics.description: The style can be distinguished from an act based on satire, or political humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insult comedy focuses on direct personal or group insults rather than the indirect critique, social commentary, or systemic critique typical of satire or political humor. Material should be judged by whether its intent is to insult/tease individuals/groups rather than to satirize institutions or policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical use against hecklers
rubrics_metrics.description: Insult comedy is often used to deflect or silence hecklers even when the rest of the show is not focused on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical function of insult-comedy techniques is to handle interruptions or hostile audience members; performers may deploy quick insult routines situationally to regain control of a set. The article notes this use explicitly.
